scientific_integrity: The heterogeneous sharp parameter follows by recomputing the exact total Gaussian variance in the published product and applying the equal-variance Gaussian trade-off argument used in the source product theorem. The privacy-utility invariant and constrained frontier are then exact algebraic consequences. Targeted statement-level comparisons were made against the motivating GDP e-value paper, prior private e-value product results under Renyi DP, foundational GDP, and semantic database searches; an unindexed equivalent observation remains a residual originality risk.
scientific_limitations: The result assumes mutually independent disjoint blocks, strictly positive e-values with finite positive log sensitivities, independent canonical Gaussian perturbations with fixed block-specific GDP parameters, and publication only of the scalar product. It does not cover correlated noise, overlapping records, data-dependent privacy allocation, non-Gaussian mechanisms, separate factor release, or downstream power optimality.
title: A privacy–utility invariant and sharp heterogeneous-budget frontier for product Gaussian private e-values
